summary.text: Val Hoyle is the Democratic U.S. Representative for Oregon's 4th Congressional District, which she has represented since January 2023, and won re-election on November 3, 2026, according to unofficial results. Before Congress she spent 25 years in the international bicycle industry, then served in the Oregon House of Representatives, including as Majority Leader, and as Oregon's Labor Commissioner. In the U.S. House she sits on the Transportation and Infrastructure and Natural Resources committees.

paragraphs.text: Hoyle was born on Travis Air Force Base in Fairfield, California. According to her office, her father was a firefighter and labor leader and her mother organized in support of the 1972 Equal Rights Amendment. Ballotpedia lists her birth year as 1964.

She was the first in her family to earn a college degree, beginning at Bunker Hill Community College and graduating from Emmanuel College with a bachelor's degree in political science and a concentration in international studies; Ballotpedia lists the degree year as 1992.

Hoyle spent 25 years working in the international bicycle industry in retail management, manufacturing distribution and international trade. Ballotpedia also lists work as a director at United Way of Lane County and as a policy fellow at the Wayne Morse Center for Law and Politics.
She served in the Oregon House of Representatives for West Eugene and Junction City (District 14) until 2017, and was House Majority Leader from 2013 to 2015, according to Ballotpedia.
In 2016 she ran in the Democratic primary for Oregon Secretary of State and finished second to Brad Avakian.
Hoyle won the nonpartisan Oregon Commissioner of Labor and Industries primary outright in May 2018 and served as Labor Commissioner, leading the Bureau of Labor and Industries, from 2019 to 2023.

Hoyle won the open 4th District seat in November 2022, succeeding Peter DeFazio, and was sworn into the 118th Congress in January 2023. She was re-elected in 2024 over Republican Monique DeSpain and Pacific Green Justin Filip.

She serves on the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and the House Committee on Natural Resources, and belongs to caucuses including the Congressional Progressive Caucus, New Democrat Coalition and Labor Caucus.
According to her office, she and her husband Stephen are both union members and moved to Lane County more than 25 years ago to raise their two children.
She won the November 3, 2026 general election with 53.7% of the vote to Monique DeSpain's 42.8% and Justin Filip's 3.4%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
